chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If he had not yet consummated the marriage with her, and he had obligated a dower for her, then she is entitled to half of what he obligated for her, and she is entitled to inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period.
ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a widow if her husband died before consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the status of a widow in the intermediate stage between contract and consummation, a key distinction in Shia fiqh that grants her full inheritance rights unlike the half-dower rule for non-consummated but not yet married cases. It underscores the principle that the marital bond is sufficiently established upon the contract to trigger inheritance and iddah, even if physical union has not occurred. This ruling reflects the juristic consensus that the 'right of consummation' (haqq al-dakhil) is the threshold for full spousal privileges.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘If she did not happen to have been slept with, and the dower was obligated for her, so for her is half of what had been obligated for her, and for her is the inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one has not gone to bed with his wife but has set up mahr (dower), she deserves one-half of the mahr (dower) that is set for her and complete inheritance. She must count complete waiting period.’”
